about: What is known of each SOLIDWORKS API member (entry U1.1). Read by api_signature and api_search; checked by the contracts: every member must exist in the interop, every enum map must name a real parameter and a real swconst enum, measured types only on parameters declared Object, indices only on "return" or a real parameter. A member that is not here is never_probed. Enum maps and index meanings are written only when known: anything else is "enum not tabulated" / "index not tabulated".

states.forbidden: never called by the bridge (crash, modal, arbitrary code, the whole application)
states.confirm: writes to disk or does what cannot be undone: asks a person first
states.gray: called and measured to lie, return nothing usable or behave only sometimes
states.probed_read: called and measured: reads, does not modify
states.probed_modifies: called and measured: modifies the model

IAssemblyDoc.AddComponent5.why: Takes a path on disk (the document must already be saved). Measured 2026-09-17 and predicted beforehand: positions the CENTER of the component's bounding box, NOT its origin. A part extruded in one direction only (the normal case) has its origin on a face, not mid-thickness: asked for z=30 on a 4mm-thick part, the origin lands at (0,-2,30); asked for z=0 on a 10mm-thick part, origin lands at (0,-5,0) -- both predicted before probing and confirmed after. Report the field as origine_mm, not posizione_mm (the two rarely coincide and the old name invited a wrong comparison).

IAssemblyDoc.AddMate5.why: 15 arguments, mostly Double/Int32/Boolean positional -- a position mistake mates silently, no exception. Measured 2026-09-17: no special "selection mark" is needed (that unknown, once rated 8-10h, turned out to not exist): plain IEntity.Select4(append:true, null) on the two entities, then AddMate5, answers swAddMateError_NoError. IMPORTANT: in swAddMateError_e, NoError = 1 and ErrorUnknown = 0 -- a naive 'if (errore != 0)' would report a successful mate as failed. swMateAlign_e has three pairs of names on the same value: swAlignNONE = swMateAlignALIGNED = 0, swAlignSAME = swMateAlignANTI_ALIGNED = 1, swAlignAGAINST = swMateAlignCLOSEST = 2. "SAME" is worth "ANTI_ALIGNED": same number, opposite sense. The bridge writes swMateAlignANTI_ALIGNED / swMateAlignALIGNED (OperazioniAccoppia.cs:109).

IAssemblyDoc.AutoExplode.why: Boolean return, zero arguments: an innocuous-looking signature, but 'auto' with no arguments means SOLIDWORKS decides on its own, and it is not known whether it decides silently or pops a dialog. Must be measured on a throwaway document (does the call return within a few seconds?) before trusting it, not assumed either way.

IAssemblyDoc.CreateExplodedView.why: CORRECTION of an earlier note in the same source: initial reflection guessed this was a zero-arg UI-button opener like EditExplodeParameters/ViewExplodeAssembly. Actual measurement on 2026-09-17 disproved that: the call returns True and creates a real exploded view step ("Vista esplosa1"), no blocking dialog. Trust the runtime measurement over the earlier hypothesis.

IAssemblyDoc.CreateMateData.why: The Type parameter is declared Int32 and which enum it takes is NOT tabulated: reflection cannot say it, and nobody has measured it yet. Entry U11.3 measures it; until then api_signature says "enum not tabulated".

IAssemblyDoc.EditExplodeParameters.why: Void return, zero arguments: pattern already paid for with AddDimension/ManuallySelect/Select4(ShowPopup:true) -- a zero-arg Void member is a UI button with nobody on the other end to click OK. Never actually called; flagged from reflection alone, not run.

IAssemblyDoc.GetComponents.why: Call with false, not true. With true, a sub-assembly comes back as ONE component with nothing inside, and the model would read '2 components' on an assembly that really has thirty -- every reasoning built on that count would be plausible and wrong.

IAssemblyDoc.ReplaceComponents2.why: Measured 2026-09-17 in six conditions (assembly saved/unsaved, new file opened/closed): with ReAttachMates=true AND a component that has real mates to reattach, the call raises RPC_E_SERVERFAULT. With ReAttachMates=false it always succeeds. Always pass false; a probe that only checks the call succeeds (not whether mates survive) is not proof either way -- the bench found 0 mates lost with false, the opposite of what a shallow probe suggested.

IAssemblyDoc.ViewExplodeAssembly.why: Same reasoning as EditExplodeParameters: Void, zero arguments, suspected UI-only entry point. Never actually called.

IBody2.Check.why: Measured: 1 on a sound solid, 1 on two touching solids, 1 on an open sheet body. OPPOSITE convention to Check2 (0 on the same sound body). Does not see an open sheet.

IBody2.Check2.why: Measured: 0 on a sound solid, 0 on two touching solids, 0 on an open sheet body. OPPOSITE convention to Check (1 on the same sound body): reading 0 as "false, broken" gives a stable, coherent, inverted answer.

IBody2.DeleteFaces2.why: Real 'Delete Face' with reconstruction option (Object/typed Face2[] argument family); not yet exercised. Needs IDeleteFaceFeatureData for reread.

IBody2.DeleteFaces3.why: Same family as DeleteFaces2; not yet exercised.

IBody2.DeleteFaces4.why: Same family as DeleteFaces2; not yet exercised.

IBody2.DeleteFaces5.why: Has extra HealAction/LoopProcessOption parameters -- SUSPECTED (by having the highest number and the richest parameter set) to be the one to promote, but this is exactly the 'last of a /2/3/4/5 family, not verified' case: not yet exercised, do not assume it is correct without measuring.

IBody2.Diagnose.why: Returns DiagnoseResult; IDiagnoseResult.GetGapsCount() is the only one of the four checks that sees an open sheet body (1 gap, where Check, Check2 and Check3 all say sound).

IBody2.GetMassProperties.why: Returns a double[] (declared Object). MEASURED index 3 = volume in cubic meters: on 2026-09-09, eleven guided-hole sizes M3 through M24 all matched pi*r^2*depth at the tenth of a cubic millimeter using index 3. IMPORTANT: a member named IBody2.GetVolume does NOT exist in the inventory -- it is one of several names that 'sounded right' and were not; GetMassProperties(density) is the real member. GetBodies2 (needed to get the IBody2 instances) lives on IPartDoc, not on IModelDoc2.

return.3: volume, cubic metres (measured 9/9/2026 on eleven guided holes M3-M24)
return.0-2: centre of mass, metres (used by green bench cases: volume-weighted centre of several bodies)

IBody2.GetUpdateStamp.why: Candidate generation counter for object-registry staleness (U1.2). NOT yet measured whether it changes on a plain selection (SelectByID2/Select4) alone -- if it does, every preselection would immediately expire the entities just registered, and would block U7 (which lives on preselection). This measurement is the actual point of U1.2, not yet done.

IBody2.get_Check3.why: A PROPERTY returning FaultEntity, not a method: written Check3() in late binding it fails at run time inside a catch. Measured: Check3.Count is 0 on a sound solid, on two touching solids AND on an open sheet body: it does not see an open sheet. Only IBody2.Diagnose().GetGapsCount() does.

IBomTableAnnotation.SaveAsExcel.why: Writes an Excel file to disk.

IComponent2.GetMates.why: Returns Object (an array of mate references) but returns NULL when there are zero mates, NOT an empty array -- this is the convention on much of this API. A null return can mean either "zero mates" or "could not read": tell them apart by checking whether the component still answers its own Name2 (alive -> null really means zero; unresponsive -> null means unknown).

IComponent2.GetPathName.why: Used to detect the no-op case of replacing a component with itself (same resolved full path).

IComponent2.GetRemainingDOFs.why: Does NOT return a count. Returns a swRemainingDofs_e STATE (Restricted=0, Unrestricted=1, Unavailable=2, Failed=3, RootComponent=4). Measured 2026-09-16: a freshly built assembly returns 2 (Unavailable) identically for a FIXED component and a FREE component -- the same value on two different truths means the value tabulates nothing. Do not publish it as a DOF count; use IsFixed() + GetMates() count instead.

IComponent2.GetTotalTransform.why: Returns an IMathTransform (declared Object). Argument true INCLUDES the exploded-view transform if one exists and is shown -- a position read with true while exploded is the exploded-view position, plausible and wrong; check IModelDocExtension.IsExploded first. See IMathTransform.ArrayData for how to read the returned transform.

IComponent2.IsFixed.why: Reliable. Measured: SOLIDWORKS itself fixes the FIRST component inserted into a new assembly (base-1 fixed=True vs coperchio-1 fixed=False) -- every assembly therefore has at least one pinned part, and a DOF sum that does not exclude fixed components would be wrong on every assembly, always, in the convenient direction nobody checks.

IComponent2.get_Name2.why: Unique within the assembly ("base-1", "base-2", "coperchio-1"), and this is what makes a stable C1..Cn numbering possible: sort by Name2, never trust GetComponents' own return order, which is not documented anywhere and was seen to differ between reads.

IConfiguration.AddExplodeStep2.why: Has an out Error parameter carrying swAddExplodeStepError_e -- the error is NOT in the return value. Measured 2026-09-17: on a freshly built assembly, returned NoComponents(3) across five different selection attempts (whole component, one at a time, various Select4/ManuallySelect variants); the correct selection recipe to make a step succeed is still unmeasured.

IConfiguration.GetExplodeStep.why: Measured working: step 0 named "Catena1", 2 components, distance 0 mm in that run.

IConfiguration.get_ChildComponentDisplay.why: Second of the two BOM-opening fields, same caveat as get_ShowChildComponentsInBOM.

IConfiguration.get_ShowChildComponentsIn.why: One of two BOM fields (out of six total on IConfiguration) that decide whether a sub-assembly OPENS in the BOM; found by reflection, not measured at runtime. A sub-assembly that opens when it should not adds unrequested rows and the BOM stays plausible but wrong.

ICurve.CircleParams.why: Returns a double[] (declared Object). The slots below are the ones the code reads and green bench cases check (thread diameter = [6] x 2000 mm, centre marks, hole callouts); the other slots are not tabulated.

IDeleteFaceFeatureData.GetDeletedFaces.why: Rereads the result of an IBody2.DeleteFaces* call; not yet exercised since DeleteFaces2-5 themselves are unprobed.

IDeleteFaceFeatureData.get_Options.why: Same status as GetDeletedFaces: paired reread member, not yet exercised.

IDesignTable.SaveAsExcelFile.why: Writes an Excel file to disk.

IDiagnoseResult.GetGapsCount.why: Measured: 0 on a sound solid and on two touching solids, 1 on an open sheet body. The criterion for "closed" (TODO U point 2).

IEntity.Select4.why: Measured 2026-09-17: Select4(append:true, null) on two entities is sufficient before AddMate5, no special selection mark needed. CAUTION: with ShowPopup:true this becomes a UI-button call (same family as AddDimension) -- do not set that flag from the bridge. Also: ISketchPoint/ISketchSegment are NOT IEntity (an 'as IEntity' cast silently returns null); they have their own Select4/Select2.

IEquationMgr.Add3.why: Reliable, unlike get_Status: returns the new equation's index, or -1 on failure. Also measured: an equation variable named 'spessore' or 'Spessore' is REJECTED even on a part with no such property, and silently binds to an unrelated value (3) instead of raising an error -- these are reserved words in the Italian SOLIDWORKS UI. Use a non-reserved example name (e.g. 'parete') and always reread the value.

IEquationMgr.EvaluateAll.why: The call itself does something real, but its own get_Status afterward lies (-1 even on success) -- always reread the actual driven values, never trust Status.

IEquationMgr.get_Status.why: MEASURED 2026-09-27 to be unusable as a success/failure signal: reads -1 after a successful EvaluateAll AND reads 1 after a successful set_Equation -- it does not track outcome. Never branch on it; instead reread get_Value and the driven dimension after any write.

IEquationMgr.set_Equation.why: Same get_Status caveat as EvaluateAll (reads 1 even on a successful write -- not a useful confirmation). Also subject to the 'spessore' reserved-name trap under Add3.

IExplodeStep.ExplodeDistance.why: Reading (get_ExplodeDistance) is safe and measured working (0 mm on a freshly created, not-yet-dragged step). WARNING: the SETTER of this same property, set_ExplodeDistance, is a separate forbidden entry -- writing it from out of process killed SOLIDWORKS (see IExplodeStep.set_ExplodeDistance).

IExplodeStep.GetComponentName.why: Measured working, part of reading a step's content (a step is read, not just counted).

IExplodeStep.GetNumOfComponents.why: Measured working, read alongside get_Name/get_ExplodeDistance/GetComponentName to describe a step without assuming its content.

IExplodeStep.set_ExplodeDistance.why: Measured 2026-09-26 evening: writing this property from out of process on a step created by CreateExplodedView raised 0x800706BE ("RPC server unavailable") and killed the SLDWORKS process, with the user's own session open since 24/9. Never write it out of process.

IFeature.GetUpdateStamp.why: Same open question as IBody2.GetUpdateStamp/IModelDoc2.GetUpdateStamp: which of the three stamps changes on selection alone is not yet measured.

IFeatureManager.EditDeleteFace.why: This is the reconstructive face delete/replace (with Refill option), a DIFFERENT operation from the real 'Delete Face with surface reconstruction' which lives on IBody2.DeleteFaces2-5. Not yet exercised.

IFeatureManager.FeatureExtrusion3.why: 23 positional arguments. The end conditions T1/T2 are swEndConditions_e and the start condition T0 is swStartConditions_e (the code passes them by enum name). The U1 acceptance plate (100x60x10 = 60,000 mm3) is built with it.

IFeatureManager.InsertCosmeticWeldBead.why: Measured 2026-09-25: works only via selection (the 'lato'/side variant), ONE face per side, and does NOT check whether the faces actually touch -- it will create a bead between faces that are far apart if that is not checked first.

IFeatureManager.InsertCosmeticWeldBead2.why: Measured null in EVERY form tried (object[], Face2[], and other argument variants) -- never actually created a bead in any tried combination, unlike the older InsertCosmeticWeldBead(lato).

IFeatureManager.InsertGussetFeature.why: Part of '16 null variants across three calls' (this member plus …2 and …3) all failing to create a gusset feature (GP20); suspected to need a registered macro rather than more blind argument probing.

IFeatureManager.InsertGussetFeature2.why: Same '16 null variants' family as InsertGussetFeature/InsertGussetFeature3.

IFeatureManager.InsertGussetFeature3.why: Same '16 null variants' family; also the last-numbered member of this small family (2 is the only intermediate, no 4/5 exist in the inventory).

IFeatureManager.InsertMacroFeature.why: Macro feature: code that runs on every rebuild, saved inside the part.

IFeatureManager.InsertSewRefSurface.why: Real signature confirmed by reflection: 5 arguments, returns Feature. This is the 'real' SewRefSurface the U1.1 acceptance example expects api_search("SewRefSurface") to surface alongside the old-interface Void one below.

IFeatureManager.InsertSheetMetalGussetFe.why: Distinct member from the weldment InsertGussetFeature* family above: this is the SHEET-METAL gusset (swFmSMGusset=118). GP20 only tried the weldment family; this one has not been tried at all yet and should be tried before assuming it shares the same failure.

IFeatureManager.InsertWeldmentCutList2.why: Named in the same object[]-vs-typed-array trap family as InsertWeldmentTrimFeature2 (both take Body2[]/Face2[]-shaped Object parameters), but this member's own volume/tree measurement has not been independently confirmed the way InsertWeldmentTrimFeature2 was -- treat the typed-array requirement as certain by family, the exact phantom-feature numbers as unconfirmed for this specific member.

measured_types.Bodies: Body2[] by family with InsertWeldmentTrimFeature2 (not measured on this member)

IFeatureManager.InsertWeldmentTrimFeatur.why: MEASURED 2026-09-25 on a two-member weldment frame (taglia_membri): with object[] for BodiesToTrim/BodiesOrFaces the interop marshals a VARIANT array and SOLIDWORKS answers with a feature that never enters the tree -- part unchanged, NO error at all. With Body2[] typed arrays (or DispatchWrapper[]) the cut is real: volume drops by the expected -58798.23 mm3. This is the cardinal defense of the whole bridge (U1.3): arguments must always be converted to the type the signature declares.

measured_types.BodiesToTrim: Body2[] (DispatchWrapper[] also works; object[] makes a phantom feature)
measured_types.BodiesOrFaces: Body2[] or Face2[] (DispatchWrapper[] also works; object[] makes a phantom feature)

IFrame.GetHWnd.why: Combined with the Win32 IsWindowEnabled call on this handle, correctly detects an open modal dialog on the main frame in 0 ms, measured 6 readings out of 6 correct (vs. CommandInProgress, wrong on 3/6). This is the guard to use, not CommandInProgress.

IMassProperty.PrincipleMomentsOfInertia.why: Measured: answers three zeros on a 200,000 mm3 steel cube. A believable wrong number: never read it; use IModelDocExtension.GetMassProperties slots 6-8.

IMassProperty2.PrincipalMomentsOfInertia.why: Measured: answers three zeros on a 200,000 mm3 steel cube, like the old spelling on IMassProperty. Use IModelDocExtension.GetMassProperties slots 6-8.

IMathTransform.ArrayData.why: 16 numbers. Measured layout: indices 0-8 are the 3x3 rotation matrix stored ROW-MAJOR (row i = indices 3i, 3i+1, 3i+2); indices 9-11 are the translation; index 12 onward: index not tabulated. IMPORTANT: the plane-normal use case measured that the normal is the THIRD ROW (indices 6,7,8), not the third column -- on two of three test planes row and column gave the same answer (50/50 chance of picking the wrong one forever), the third (oblique) plane exposed the difference: row gives the correct (0,-.7071,.7071), column gives the wrong (0,.7071,.7071). Separately, on IComponent2.GetTotalTransform, indices 9-11 were confirmed as translation by asking for z=30 and reading back [0,-2,30] (see IAssemblyDoc.AddComponent5 for the -2 explanation) and predicting+confirming a second case at (0,-5,0).

return.0-8: 3x3 rotation, row-major (row i = 3i..3i+2); a plane normal is the THIRD ROW 6-8 (measured on an oblique plane, 16/9/2026)
return.9-11: translation, metres (measured on IComponent2.GetTotalTransform: z = 30 mm read back as [0, -2, 30] mm)

IModelDoc.AddDimension.why: Old interface, same family as IModelDocExtension.AddDimension/IModelDoc2.AddDimension2 (modal + forbidden by GP6 contract). Never exposed.

IModelDoc.AddDimension2.why: Old interface, forbidden family. Never exposed.

IModelDoc.EditDelete.why: Old interface, same forbidden family as IModelDoc2.EditDelete: asks for confirmation and can bring SOLIDWORKS down. Never exposed anyway (old interface).

IModelDoc.IAddDimension2.why: Old interface, forbidden family. Never exposed.

IModelDoc2.AddDimension.why: Forbidden by contract GP6 (Prove.Contratti). Also measured unreliable even when called: returns null for sketch-point+model-edge in all four directions, and for point-to-point dimensions; use AddHorizontalDimension2/AddVerticalDimension2/AddSpecificDimension instead.

IModelDoc2.AddDimension2.why: Forbidden by contract GP6. Measured to work when called directly (e.g. 30 degrees on 30 exact, 25/9), which is exactly why it is blocked by static contract before reaching the bench.

IModelDoc2.AddHorizontalDimension2.why: Measured reliable replacement for AddDimension/AddDimension2 between a sketch point and a model edge (20mm and 30mm exact, 25/9) and between silhouettes (measures from the CENTER). Direction is chosen by the sketch edge's OWN direction: a vertical edge in the sketch takes a horizontal dimension, not the reverse -- e.g. on the right-hand face, sketch x_mm corresponds to model Y.

IModelDoc2.AddVerticalDimension2.why: Same family and same measured reliability as AddHorizontalDimension2 -- direction chosen from the sketch edge's own orientation, not assumed.

IModelDoc2.BreakAllExternalReferences.why: Destructive: severs all external references, only inside U0's sandbox folder.

IModelDoc2.EditDelete.why: Forbidden by contract (ProveLeFirmeVietate). Measured still alive in the codebase on 2026-09-27: OperazioniTabellaFori.cs:358 called modello.EditDelete() to remove a wrongly-created hole table; must be replaced with IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2 as already done in OperazioniSw.cs:5852.

IModelDoc2.GetUpdateStamp.why: Same open question: not yet measured whether this changes for reasons other than a real rebuild (e.g. mere selection).

IModelDoc2.IAddDimension2.why: Same forbidden family as AddDimension2 (typed I-variant).

IModelDoc2.InsertHelix.why: Void return, ten positional parameters, four of which (Reversed, Clockwised, Tapered, Outward) are ALL contiguous Booleans -- exactly the 'wrong but plausible number' risk pattern if two are swapped, since a mixed-up pair would not raise an error, it would just build a different helix. Correct owner found by reflection (IModelDoc2, not IFeatureManager, correcting an earlier TODO assumption) but never actually called.

IModelDoc2.InsertOffsetSurface.why: Confirmed Void return by reflection -- the exact U1.1 acceptance example of a member whose new feature is only found via the before/after photo (FotoDelPezzo), never from its own return value. Not runtime-measured beyond the signature.

IModelDoc2.InsertSewRefSurface.why: Same name as IFeatureManager.InsertSewRefSurface but zero arguments, returns Void -- the exact 'same name, two different real signatures' trap named in the U1.1 acceptance example (api_search must return both, not collapse to one).

IModelDoc2.Save.why: Writes to disk; rule 'every Save*/SaveAs* asks for human confirmation'.

IModelDoc2.SaveAs.why: Writes a (possibly new) file to disk.

IModelDoc2.SaveAs3.why: Same rule as SaveAs. This is the exact member on which api/save_denied_writes_nothing is specified (denied confirmation -> File.Exists false).

IModelDoc2.SaveAsSilent.why: Same rule as SaveAs (silent still writes to disk).

IModelDoc2.SaveBMP.why: Writes an image file to disk.

IModelDocExtension.AddDimension.why: Measured 2026-09-11: opens the "Modifica" modal dialog and the COM call never returns while swInputDimValOnCreate is on. Also measured to return null in every sketch-point+model-edge combination tried, and for point-to-point (arc centers) dimensions, and for two silhouette entities. This is exactly the AddDimension the U1.4 forbidden list names.

IModelDocExtension.AddSpecificDimension.why: Measured the ONLY working way to dimension an angle between a sketch line and a model edge (30 degrees measured exact, using swAngularDimension) after both Extension.AddDimension and AddDimension2 failed/were forbidden for that combination. On an arc, the dimension it creates is the RADIUS.

IModelDocExtension.DeleteSelection2.why: Destructive deletion, needs confirmation; is also the correct replacement for the forbidden EditDelete (used already in OperazioniSw.cs:5852 with a before/after table count).

IModelDocExtension.GetDependencies.why: Called as GetDependencies(true,false,false,true,false): Searchflag (the 2nd argument) is FALSE since Z-C21.2-ter. MEASURED 2026-09-28 (Z-C21.3, finding L12-8): with Searchflag true, a component that is not loaded (its file renamed away) came back as a DIFFERENT file with the same name found through the search rules (the current SOLIDWORKS folder), which exists, so a missing file was not reported; false answers the path where the file was last saved. Once a true call has found that file, later false calls answer it too: never call it with true before a check of missing files. Returns a flat object[] of alternating (name, path) pairs, e.g. "zb3_base", path, "zb3_coperchio", path. MEASURED: the 4th argument (documented as ListBrokenRefs) marks NOTHING even when called on an assembly with a genuinely broken reference -- result was identical to the sane assembly. Do not rely on it to flag broken references: File.Exists on each path.

IModelDocExtension.GetMassProperties.why: Returns thirteen numbers (declared Object). Measured: the principal moments of inertia are at 6, 7, 8 (0.001387, 0.001387, 0.002667 kg m2 on a 200,000 mm3 steel cube). The other slots are not tabulated here.

return.6-8: principal moments of inertia, kg m2 (measured)

IModelDocExtension.GetObjectByPersistRef.why: Second Int32& ErrorCode parameter carries the real result. Measured (case 80z): 6 of 8 references resolved after a feature suppression, the 2 missing ones came back with ErrorCode=1 -- whether a persistent reference survives a suppression specifically is still to be re-measured before relying on it there.

IModelDocExtension.GetPersistReference3.why: Returns a byte[] blob (declared Object). Measured in version 0.1: re-found 8 out of 8 faces across all five successful modifications tried, including the three cases where a sketch-point anchor was independently lost -- persistent references are more robust than the point-based anchor for this use case.

IModelDocExtension.GetWhatsWrongCount.why: NOTE ON THE OWNER: the name suggests IAssemblyDoc, but that member does not exist there (inventory-checked); the real owner is IModelDocExtension. Measured essential for detecting a mate that SURVIVES a component replacement but goes into error (pointing at faces that no longer exist): mate count alone stayed 2-before/2-after (looked fine), while GetWhatsWrongCount went 0-before/2-after (broken). A mate that stays is not the same as a mate that works.

IModelDocExtension.IsExploded.why: Measured working: follows ShowExploded2(true, name) and reports whether the assembly is currently shown exploded, and under what view name. Needed because GetTotalTransform(true) silently returns exploded-view positions.

IModelDocExtension.IsSamePersistentID.why: Returns Int32, NOT Boolean: it is a swObjectEquality (swObjectNotSame = 0, swObjectSame = 1, swObjectUnsupported = 2). The "true 46 times out of 46" of Z-A7 does not say which of the two non-zero values it was. The decision not to use it does not change: if it was 1 it never discriminated, if it was 2 it is not supported. GetObjectByPersistReference3 + a corroborating read are used instead.

IModelDocExtension.SelectByID2.why: IMPORTANT: exists ONLY on IModelDocExtension in this interop, not on IModelDoc2 -- must be called through Extension. Used with mark strings such as "BODYFEATURE"; measured that selecting by a feature's CURRENT display name (e.g. after a rename to "Taglio-Estruso1") returns false if the code still looks for the old name ("Cut-Extrude1"), i.e. selection by name is fragile across a language/rename change. SelectByID2 exists only on IModelDocExtension (9 arguments, with Mark and Callout); the other preselection is IEntity.Select4(Boolean Append, SelectData Data).

IModelDocExtension.SetUserPreferenceTogg.why: Changes how the document's numbers are interpreted (unit-level document preferences); confirm by rule. NOTE: this is a DIFFERENT member from the guard's own internal ISldWorks.SetUserPreferenceToggle use for swInputDimValOnCreate(=10)/swShowErrorsEveryRebuild(=77), which the CallGuard flips and restores itself and is not gated by user confirmation.

IPartDoc.ExportFlatPatternView.why: Measured 2026-09-24: on a part that was never saved, opens the "Save As" dialog and the call does not return. Save the document first, or call from a separate thread with a hard timeout.

IPartDoc.GetBodies2.why: BodyType is a swBodyType_e. The state reading passes swSolidBody only (StatoDocumento), which is why surface bodies are not seen today (TODO U, point 1). Lives on IPartDoc, not IModelDoc2.

IPartDoc.SaveToFile.why: Writes to disk (e.g. flat pattern export).

IPartExplodeStep.set_ExplodeDistance.why: Same crash family as IExplodeStep.set_ExplodeDistance (sister interface on part-level explode steps).

ISilhouetteEdge.GetCurve.why: Measured to return null from out of process (does not crash like GetStartPoint/GetEndPoint, but gives nothing usable).

ISilhouetteEdge.GetFace.why: Measured null until GraphicsRedraw2 is called and the entity re-requested; even after redraw some faces on some geometries (bushings) never come back, and after a new dimension previously-read silhouettes may stop selecting.

ISilhouetteEdge.GetStartPoint.why: Measured 2026-09-27: called from out of process raises RPC_E_SERVERFAULT (SOLIDWORKS itself throws). Named explicitly in the U1.4 forbidden list.

ISldWorks.ActivateDoc.why: Measured 2026-09-14: changes the active document seen by OTHER sessions on the same SOLIDWORKS process; a test estrudi_rettangolo landed inside another session's Parte4 this way. Bridge must keep its own IModelDoc2 reference, never ActiveDoc/Activate*.

ISldWorks.AddMenu.why: Modifies the application UI for every user of this SOLIDWORKS instance.

ISldWorks.CloseAllDocuments.why: Closes documents belonging to other sessions on the same SOLIDWORKS (multiple sessions share one process, measured).

ISldWorks.CloseDoc.why: Forbidden for a document this session did not open or create (multi-session risk, measured); the bridge closes only its own documents, always discarding, never saving.

ISldWorks.ExitApp.why: Closes the whole application; other sessions/users share the same SOLIDWORKS process and license seat (K7).

ISldWorks.Frame.why: Returns the main window Object (declared Object, not a typed Frame) from which GetHWnd is obtained for the modal guard.

ISldWorks.GetAddInObject.why: From here one reaches the OpenPDM add-in and its vault.

ISldWorks.IActivateDoc2.why: Same measured risk as ActivateDoc (typed variant).

ISldWorks.IActivateDoc3.why: Same measured risk as ActivateDoc (typed variant).

ISldWorks.LoadAddIn.why: Changes what is loaded in the whole application, can reach the OpenPDM add-in and its vault.

ISldWorks.LoadFile4.why: Measured: loading a STEP file opens the modal "New SOLIDWORKS Document" dialog (model template chooser) and the call does not return until someone closes it; closed with Cancel, the import still proceeded as a 2-component assembly. Forbidden until U10 finds a way without the modal. To verify a STEP without importing, count MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP occurrences in the file text instead.

ISldWorks.RunMacro.why: Arbitrary code execution surface: forbidden by U1.4 rule regardless of family/overload.

ISldWorks.SendMsgToUser.why: Opens a modal message box; same trap family as AddDimension (blocking dialog, COM call never returns).

ISldWorks.SetUserPreferenceToggle.why: Application-wide preference, persists in the Windows registry: confirm by rule for general use. Two specific values are the known measured exception, flipped and restored automatically by the call guard itself (not user-facing confirm): swInputDimValOnCreate(=10) before any call that could pop the "Modifica" quote dialog, and swShowErrorsEveryRebuild(=77) around rebuilds, both saved to a %LOCALAPPDATA% file and mutex-guarded across processes so two overlapping bridge/bench/add-in instances cannot leave the toggle stuck off.

ISldWorks.get_ActiveDoc.why: Bridge must use its own kept obj:doc reference, never the shared ActiveDoc (multi-session risk, measured 14/9).

ISldWorks.get_CommandInProgress.why: Measured UNRELIABLE as a modal-dialog guard: stays False while a modal dialog is open (wrong on 3 of 6 readings in one run). Do not use it to detect a stuck/blocked call.

IView.AutoInsertCenterMarks2.why: Correct owner found by reflection while SOLIDWORKS was locked (23-24/9), replacing a wrong assumption in the TODO; not run/measured at runtime, only confirmed to exist with this signature.

IView.GetPolylines7.why: Returns Object (the curve objects); the out parameter Polylines (Object&) carries a positional numeric array whose slot meanings have never been measured on this project: index not tabulated, do not assume a "classic" order. Measured: on the stepped-shaft example, for the silhouette of the D20 face the object in GetPolylines7 was null.

IView.InsertWeldmentTable.why: Correct owner found by reflection while SOLIDWORKS was locked (23-24/9); not run/measured at runtime.
